success_patterns: Several passages were flashcard or archive dumps that put the clue in ALL CAPS, then a comma, then the answer and a period, then the start of the NEXT card ('...INTO THIS LANGUAGE, WELSH. POLAND'S...', '..., WALLY LAMB. THERE'S NO...', '| Emperor. right:'). The agents took only the short answer between the clue's end and the next card, and copied it as a bare entity.
For 'Title held ... by A, B & C' (Balbinus, Bao Dai & Bidatsu), the agent answered the shared role noun ('Emperor'), singular and bare, rather than a person or a country-specific title.

When the clue's descriptors recur across many independent passages directly next to one proper noun (appositive style: 'famed horticulturist Luther Burbank ... Santa Rosa plum'; 'Tick-Licker ... Daniel Boone'; 'Counting Crows ... Mr. Jones'), the agents committed to that name in its common full form with no extra descriptor or role word.

Crossword-solver pages that echo the clue ('Tick-Licker was his favorite rifle, 5 letter, 2nd letter O') gave no answer themselves. The agent used the other passages to find the entity and used the letter hints only as a sanity check (BOONE fits).
Leading articles and role words were dropped (harpsichord, radical, Welsh, Emperor), consistent with the existing formatting rules.

patch.reasoning: All 8 successes came from clues repeated nearly verbatim or from appositive sentences. The skill covers most of this already. Three gaps remain: (a) how to cut the answer out of an all-caps flashcard dump where the next card runs straight on after the answer (seen in 3 of 8), (b) 'Title/Position held by A, B & C' clues, where the answer is the shared role noun, and (c) crossword-solver pages that only echo the clue and should serve as a length/letter check, not a source. I kept the additions short and grounded in observed wins, because earlier long additions were rejected for hurting other tasks.

edits.target: - Archive lines may also be formatted 'CATEGORY | clue text | answer'. Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - Flashcard dumps (StudyStack and similar) run cards together in ALL CAPS: 'CLUE TEXT, ANSWER. NEXT CARD CLUE...'. The answer is the short phrase between the end of the clue and the next period ('...INTO THIS LANGUAGE, WELSH. POLAND'S...' -> Welsh; '..."I KNOW THIS MUCH IS TRUE", WALLY LAMB. THERE'S NO...' -> Wally Lamb). Ignore the text after that period because it belongs to another card. Write the answer in normal capitalisation, without the clue words.

edits.target: If the list is of real people, answer with the team, state or other entity they share.
edits.content: - 'Title / rank / position / role held by A, B & C' (people from different countries or eras, 'Balbinus, Bao Dai & Bidatsu') asks for the ONE role noun they all share ('Emperor'). Give it bare and singular, without a country or 'of ...' tail, and do not answer with one of the named people.

edits.target: Do not talk yourself out of a well-supported entity.
edits.content: - Appositive hits are strong evidence. When the clue's descriptors ('famed horticulturist ... Santa Rosa plum', 'favorite rifle ... Tick-Licker') appear in several independent passages right next to one proper noun, answer with that noun in its common full form ('Luther Burbank', 'Daniel Boone') and stop. Crossword-solver pages that only echo the clue, or add hints such as '5 letter, 2nd letter O', are not answer sources. Use their length and letter hints only to check a candidate.
